workPackageTitle: Architecture dependency tests plus complete documentation/requirement/component/contract/schema/verification/work ID registry validator
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91-verification-strategy.md § Verification registry).

TASK-FND-009-002 implements the structural validator for this file and for every other tests/verification/*.json, so this package validates its own registry. That is deliberate: a validator that could not be run against the registry it belongs to would leave its own package unchecked.

The architecture rules are a pure function from a ProjectGraph to findings, and the graph is a plain value a test can construct. That is what makes 'each forbidden synthetic edge fails' provable: an assertion that could only read the real repository can never be shown to fail on any edge, so it would be evidence of nothing.

build/verify-architecture.sh stays. It asks MSBuild to evaluate every project, which catches an SDK-injected package reference no project file mentions, and the build verb invokes it (BuildVerb). No CI invokes it: this repository has no .github/ directory. Of the eleven build/verify-*.sh scripts only three are invoked by a verb - verify-architecture.sh by build, verify-policies.sh by test, verify-godot.sh by godot-import - and build/verify-registry.sh and build/verify-build-identity.sh are invoked by nothing and run only by hand. The two gates deliberately do not consume each other's output, so a defect in one reader cannot hide from both.

The registry validator reports pre-existing documentation defects rather than being weakened until the repository passes. It separates errors from warnings by rule, and the rules that fire on pre-existing doc-tree defects are reported under their own exit class so they are visible instead of downgraded. See build/verify-registry.sh and the FND-009 handoff for the complete list found at implementation time.

tests/verification/FND-001.json wrote the section sign as literal UTF-8 while FND-002.json and FND-003.json wrote it as a six-character JSON escape. TASK-FND-009-002 normalizes every registry file on literal UTF-8, because .editorconfig already fixes charset = utf-8 for the whole repository and an escape only obscures a character the file is already required to encode. The validator enforces it, and this note deliberately describes the escape in words rather than writing it, because writing it here would violate the rule the note is about.

VER-FND-009-010 and VER-FND-009-011 originally cited a MechaMiner.Tools.Tests.Audit.VerificationRegistryTests fixture that was never written, while carrying status: implemented. The validator could not see it: its selector check compared only the namespace prefix against the list of test projects, so any class or method name after that prefix passed. Both entries are repointed to RegistryValidatorTests, the narrowest node containing every test each claim depends on - the real-tree assertion (TheRepositoryHasNoIdentifierErrors, which is where a registry-shape or section-sign violation in any tests/verification/*.json becomes an error) and the negative control over the malformed fixture (TheMalformedFixtureProvesTheRegistryShapeRules). Neither status was weakened: the rules were always real and running, only the citation was false. VER-FND-009-014 registers the check that would have caught it.

VER-FND-009-010 carries negative-control among its evidence kinds, and each of the three claims its summary makes beyond the entry shape now has a control of its own. The VER-<WORK-PACKAGE>-### grammar: RegistryValidatorTests.ARegistryWhoseDeclaredIdentityDisagreesWithItsFileIsRejected, three cases - an entry ID belonging to another package, a wrong schema, and a workPackage that disagrees with the file name. Non-compilation verification per task: ATaskWhoseOnlyEvidenceIsCompilationIsRejected, over an entry whose evidenceKinds is exactly [compilation]. Ordinals: EntryOrdinalsThatAreNotTheDeclaredSequenceAreRejected, two cases - a descending pair and a gap - because ValidateNumbering has two loops and each returns after its first finding. Before those controls existed, deleting RegistryIdentityMismatch, RegistryNumbering or TaskWithoutVerification from Validate left the whole suite green, so this entry claimed a control that did not exist; deleting any of them now fails only that rule's own controls. All three run over a composed two-entry fixture registry document whose unmutated form is asserted to produce nothing, so a validator that had broken into rejecting every registry would fail rather than pass.

VER-FND-009-010's last clause was narrowed rather than left standing. It claimed 'no entry is renumbered relative to the committed registry', which RegistryNumbering does not check: the rule compares a file's ordinals against the sequence 1..n and never looks at the previously committed file, so renumbering every entry uniformly would satisfy it. Detecting that would need a committed baseline of per-entry ordinals, which is a separate mechanism and not one this task built. The clause now states what the rule enforces.

VER-FND-009-013 is a negative control of a gate, not of the product. It was added when MechaMiner.Diagnostics became a sixth src/ project: build/verify-architecture.sh gained the row that keeps that project a dependency leaf, and nothing yet showed the script's comparison could reject a violation of it. The five fixtures live under build/policy-fixtures/architecture/ beside the build-policy fixtures, because they are the same kind of evidence - a deliberately invalid input that must fail - and are deliberately not members of MechaMiner.sln.

entries.summary: The real repository satisfies the accepted project boundary: solution membership, every project-reference edge, the Godot dependency, the source scans, and the prescribed layout all produce zero findings.

Every forbidden project-reference edge fails, proved one negative control per edge: the complete ordered-pair matrix of accepted projects is enumerated, the pairs doc 115 permits are skipped, and each remaining pair is injected alone into an otherwise fully compliant graph and must produce exactly its own finding. A reference to MechaMiner.Game is reported as a reverse Godot edge rather than an ordinary forbidden one.
fixtures: synthetic ProjectGraph, one forbidden edge per control

entries.summary: A Godot dependency in any project the boundary forbids one in fails, proved per project and per kind of evidence (SDK attribute, package reference, lock-file entry); the Godot project losing its engine dependency also fails; a Godot import outside game/ fails; and a GDScript file fails.
fixtures: synthetic ProjectGraph with injected Godot evidence, Godot import, or GDScript file

entries.summary: A permitted-but-undeclared reference edge is reported as drift under its own rule rather than as a boundary violation, and a declared edge that disappears from a project file is reported as missing. Both matter because doc 115 states a maximum while the repository has an exact current set, and collapsing the two would let legal-but-unannounced dependency growth pass silently.
Every prescribed repository layout path is individually load-bearing: removing any one of them from the observed layout fails, proved per path rather than by one sample.

Solution membership must match the accepted decomposition exactly: omitting an accepted project and adding an unaccepted one are each rejected under distinct rules, and a project file on disk that the decomposition does not name is rejected as well. A compliant graph produces no findings at all, so the negative controls measure the injected violation rather than a rule that always fires.

Every CMP-*, CTR-*, SCH-*, TR-*, TDR-*, VER-*, work-package, and TASK-* identifier in the specification and the verification registries is unique, is defined exactly once, and resolves wherever it is referenced.
Missing, duplicate, dangling, and malformed identifier fixtures each fail, under their own distinct rule, proved with one fixture per class so a single sample cannot stand for all four.

Every relative document cross-link and every in-document anchor a technical document references resolves to a file that exists and to a heading that exists, and a broken link or a dangling anchor fails.

Every tests/verification/*.json file validates against the SCH-QUA-001 shape doc 91 § Verification registry prescribes: a stable VER-<WORK-PACKAGE>-### ID, summary, cited TR-* requirements and sources, an automated selector or a manual procedure ID, fixture/seed/scenario IDs, evidence kinds, platforms, tier, and status. Every implementation task named by any entry has at least one non-compilation verification, and entry ordinals are the sequence 1..n in ascending order, so an entry cannot be reordered or deleted without the descent or the gap being reported.

Every registry file encodes the section sign as literal UTF-8 rather than a JSON escape, normalized across all of tests/verification/, and a file that escapes it fails. The repository already fixes charset = utf-8 in .editorconfig, so an escape only hides a character the file must encode anyway, and two spellings in sibling files make textual review and diffing inconsistent.

The registry validator is reachable through the existing command surface and returns a doc 100 exit class: build/verify-registry.sh runs it, structural errors return class 4, and pre-existing documentation defects are reported under a distinct diagnostic code rather than downgraded to warnings so they cannot be silently accumulated.

build/verify-architecture.sh's own boundary comparisons are proved capable of failing. Sections 3 and 4 previously ran only against compliant projects, so a broken comparison would have gone on printing ok; MechaMiner.Diagnostics made that gap load-bearing because its accepted row is the strictest in the repository and is the only thing keeping the diagnostics leaf a leaf. Four fixture projects named MechaMiner.Diagnostics.csproj, each carrying one violation of that row - a reference to MechaMiner.Content, to MechaMiner.Simulation, to MechaMiner.Game (the reverse Godot edge), and a GodotSharp PackageReference - are fed through the same edges_match and godot_matches functions the real projects use, and each must be rejected. A fifth compliant fixture must be accepted, so a comparison that reported a difference for every input could not pass the four negative controls silently. The accepted row is read out of EXPECTED_PROJECTS rather than restated, and a missing row or a missing fixture file fails rather than skipping.

Every nunit selector in every tests/verification/*.json resolves to a test the NUnit harness itself reports, so an entry cannot claim implemented coverage of test code that does not exist. The test list is discovered with dotnet test --list-tests per accepted test project rather than maintained by hand, and a selector naming a nonexistent class, or a real class with a nonexistent method, is rejected. Discovery returning zero tests is itself a failure with its own rule rather than a pass with nothing to compare against, and a control proves that guard reads the discovered-test count rather than asserting a constant: an inventory of one non-matching test must fail as an unresolved selector and not as an empty inventory.
